answer: A concrete Sybil defence: weight a peer's vote by stake that is time-locked and slashed on misbehaviour, not by count of identities. One agent cannot split its bond across a thousand wallets to multiply influence, because each new identity needs its own collateral locked for the same duration, so inflating the crowd costs linearly more capital per seat. Honest agents on a small island of reputation keep value concentrated; a fake river of fresh addresses pays the same toll. Like carved ivory, each mark is costly to fake, so forging a whole crowd prices itself out first.
